mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, indicating supply chain disruptions, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle to meet demand and earnings estimates are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment, measured by the monthly change in UNRATE, signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand that will pressure S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises by > 0.5% in a month, but SPX returns are positive over the next 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, indicating a restrictive monetary policy, S&P 500 returns tend to be negative over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs pressure corporate profits.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, but SPX returns are positive in > 60% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise by more than 10% year-over-year, indicating strong consumer demand, S&P 500 returns tend to be positive over the next 60 trading days as the housing sector boosts economic growth.
failure_condition: HOUST rises > 10% YoY, but SPX returns are negative in > 40% of the next 60-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 300,000 jobs in a month, signaling a very strong labor market, S&P 500 returns tend to be positive over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: PAYEMS rises > 300k, but SPX returns are negative in > 40% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% month-over-month, signaling a weakening consumer sector, S&P 500 returns tend to be negative over the next 5 trading days as companies adjust to lower demand.
failure_condition: RSAFS declines > 1% MoM, but SPX returns are positive in > 60% of the next 5-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month, indicating a surge in inflation, S&P 500 returns tend to be negative over the next 20 trading days as the Fed is likely to respond with monetary tightening.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% MoM, but SPX returns are positive in > 50% of the next 20-day periods.
